explain.say: Imagine following one drop of water from an ice cave high in the Himalayas all the way to the sea, 2,500 kilometres away. That is the journey of the Ganges. Look at the board. We will travel it stage by stage.

explain.say: It begins at the Gangotri Glacier, a river of ice. Meltwater pours out of an ice cave called Gaumukh, which means cow’s mouth. The start of a river is called its source. What do you think happens to the river when the ice melts fast in summer?

explain.say: In the mountains the young river is fast, narrow and noisy. It carries rocks that scrape its bed and cut deep V-shaped valleys. Can you see how steep the land is here, compared with the next stages?

explain.say: On the plains the river grows wide and slow, swinging in big loops called meanders. Tributaries, which are smaller rivers that join it, like the Yamuna, make it bigger. It flows past ancient cities like Varanasi. Can you spot the loops on the board?

explain.say: Near the sea it joins the Brahmaputra, splits into many channels and builds the world’s largest delta, with the Sundarbans mangrove forest, home of Bengal tigers. Then it reaches its mouth in the Bay of Bengal. What a journey! Wow fact: more than 400 million people live in the Ganges basin.

faq.a: The Ganges begins at the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand, India, where water flows from an ice cave called Gaumukh. There it is called the Bhagirathi; it becomes the Ganga at Devprayag, where it meets the Alaknanda.
asks: What is the source of the Ganges?

faq.q: Why is a river fast and narrow in the mountains?
faq.a: In the mountains the land is steep, so gravity pulls the water down fast. The fast water and the rocks it carries cut downward, making narrow V-shaped valleys, rapids and waterfalls.
A meander is a big bend in a river on flat land. Water flows fastest round the outside of the bend and wears the bank away, while slow water on the inside drops sand, so the bend slowly grows.
asks: Why do rivers bend on the plains?

faq.a: A delta is new land built at a river mouth from mud and sand the river drops as it slows down. The Ganges–Brahmaputra delta is the largest in the world, and its Sundarbans are the largest mangrove forest.
asks: Where does the Ganges meet the sea?

faq.a: The Ganges is about 2,525 km long. It flows through India and Bangladesh, where it is called the Padma, before reaching the Bay of Bengal.
asks: Which countries does the Ganges flow through?

facts: The Ganges is about 2,525 km long.
The Ganges–Brahmaputra delta is the largest river delta in the world.
The Sundarbans, shared by India and Bangladesh, is the largest mangrove forest in the world.

quiz.say: What is the start of a river called?
quiz.show: The start of a river is its…
quiz.why: The source is where a river begins, like the Gangotri Glacier for the Ganges.

wrong.1: The mouth is where a river ends, at the sea or a lake.
wrong.2: A delta is land built at the mouth of a river.

quiz.say: What does the Ganges do when it reaches the flat plains?
quiz.show: On the flat plains, the Ganges…

options.show: Slows down and bends in meanders
options.say: Slows down and bends in meanders

options.show: Speeds up and cuts V-shaped valleys
options.say: Speeds up and cuts V-shaped valleys

quiz.why: On flat land the river is wide and slow and swings in big loops called meanders.

wrong.1: V-shaped valleys are cut by fast water in the steep mountains.
wrong.2: The Ganges flows above ground all the way to the sea.
